answer: Admission to the agent network requires an irreversible burn of 1,000 tokens per identity to secure registry entry. The protocol verifier checks the ledger for existing burn proofs, ensuring each 1,000 unit cost is unique. An honest agent pays once, while an attacker attempting 1,000 fakes must burn 1,000,000 tokens. To maintain a prism of integrity, the system audits for address reuse. A quartz shard acts as the tamper-evident record, while a meadow of activity logs identifies clones. Detected duplicates trigger a total asset slash.
